title: Mapping the Mind: AI, EEG & the Jhana States
content:
The Consciousness Lunch & Learn series invites researchers, technologists, philosophers, meditators, and curious minds into conversations exploring the frontiers of awareness, awakening, and human experience. Across the week, sessions will dive into different topics related to consciousness.

Day 3 widens the lens. Four perspectives on the rapidly forming field of awakening research come into the same room: the academic neuroscience that gives us a window into advanced meditative states, the builder-researcher work turning those insights into tools, the infrastructure layer that lets the rest of the ecosystem move, and the funder and field-builder view on where the bets actually are.

Peter Skov-Andersen presents EEG analysis of jhana meditation, including power and complexity correlates of advanced attainment and how those map onto current models like the entropic brain hypothesis. Erik Enger shares work on AI guidance for spiritual practice: tools built with Jhourney and Joe Hudson that give teachers and students more leverage between sessions, and the open question of where AI should and shouldn't go in contemplative work. Eddy Vaisberg speaks to the spirit tech ecosystem from the builder's seat: the gap between consciousness research and the infrastructure builders need to bring this work into the world. Kati Devaney (Consciousness Foundation) closes with the view from grant-making and field-formation: where the money, the talent, and the gaps actually are.

Hosted by: Peter Skov-Andersen (Sacha Lab, Harvard), Erik Enger Karlson, Eddy Vaisberg, and Kathryn "Kati" Devaney (Consciousness Foundation).

title: The First Blinded Experiment on Marijuana Strains!
content:
Do you think you can feel the difference between an indica and a sativa strain?

For the first time ever, we are putting this question to the test scientifically. Believe it or not, this has never been done before in a blinded experiment. (The closest thing was a 2023 study in which participants chose what to smoke and they were aware of what strain they were ingesting, so the effects of the strain cannot be distinguished from the influence of participant’s expectations about how it should feel.) 

People claim that different strains of marijuana create different effects. It is commonly believed that sativas are uplifting and indicas are relaxing. This could be a story we tell ourselves, or the dispensary sommeliers (“ganjier”) may be truly able to detect subtle variations. Whether or not the strains produce genuinely different effects under blinded conditions, there is an opportunity to better understand the true potential of Cannabis strain specialization.

This study also more generally speaks to the question of how our expectations of a mind-altering experience actually affect our experience. For example, people commonly report similar visions of jaguars and serpents while on ayahuasca (MAPS), but how much of this is due to what they have heard they should expect? It is impossible to run a blinded experiment on such a powerful drug. But with different marijuana strains we have the opportunity to compare how societally-given expectations may influence one’s substance use experience.

For more context on this study, see the original proposal (which has been slightly modified for this context): https://cosimoresearch.substack.com/p/proposal-the-first-blinded-study

During this session, each participant will smoke 2 puffs of a randomly assigned joint (you will not know what kind), and 30 minutes later you will fill out a brief survey about how you feel and what you think you smoked. Join us for a smoke sesh and contribute to novel scientific research!

title: Tactile Anatomy: How To Feel Your Organs
content:
Our organs keep us alive and in good health, but can you feel them via your sense of touch?

​Did you know that a struggling liver can feel 'boggy' and overly pliable, or that the stomach can become adhered to the diaphragm and restrict breathing?

​Come join bodyworkers Dr. Myles O'Donnell and Elena Lake for 90 minutes of organ stories! Elena will host, and Myles will share locations, functions, and textural cues for various abdominal organs, as well as stories of interacting with them in their practice.

​Both Myles and Elena practice a form of organ-focused bodywork called visceral manipulation, which fills in a big blindspot of muscular-centric modalities.

​Our organs straightforwardly store mechanical tensions which transmit to other places in our body - hips, shoulders, neck, even toes if you can sense precisely enough. Myles will demo some releases on audience volunteers, and there will also be time for Q&A.

​We will cover some subset of: the lungs, the heart, the esophagus and stomach, the pancreas, the liver, the small intestine, the large intestine, and the kidneys. We'll explore tactile cues on our own torsos, and there may be some optional partnered exercises.

Elena Lake studied math, physics, and computer science at MIT, then realized that Well-Trained Human Senses Are The Most Mathematically Rigorous Wellness Approach (quoted from her article by the same name) and pivoted to bodywork and somatic healing. 

​Here's a story from Myles's practice, as a teaser:

​I had a patient come in a while ago complaining of "carpal tunnel" and acid reflux. In my examination, when I felt their wrists and hands, there wasn't any significant tension or patterns to clear. Their carpal tunnel had nerve tension, but I could feel it pulling from upstream. When I traced the tension upward, it brought me to their ribcage and torso, where I could feel a strong distortion through their stomach and esophagus. 
The esophagus typically tethers to T2, so if there is tension in the stomach, it can create compression through the upper back/thoracic inlet which then created tension in their brachial plexus leading to a nerve sensation similar to carpal tunnel.
The lower esophageal sphincter was stuck open due to the tension pulling it up towards the head. When this sphincter is open, it lets the stomach acid travel upward and causes the burning sensation of heart burn.
When I released the upper esophagus and the adhesions between the stomach and diaphragm and chest wall, the whole stomach dropped and the lower esophageal sphincter closed and their acid reflux stopped almost instantly.

Dr. Myles DC is a somatic chiropractor specializing in somatic trauma-work, Bio-Geometric Integration, Visceral Manipulation, Craniosacral, Network Spinal, and Osteopathic Manual Therapy. They use precise somatic listening and gentle attuned touch to help untangle webs of trauma stored within the body's tissues. Their practice is in Oakland. You can read more about them and their approach here: www.somaconnectionchiro.com

title: Why We’re Rebuilding Women’s Biology in the Lab
content: At Opal Therapeutics we believe women’s biology has been overlooked in medicine for far too long. Most drugs for conditions like endometriosis and fibroids are still developed using rodent models that don't menstruate. The problem is that the data doesn't translate into effective therapies when we reach human clinical trials.  We’re rebuilding human uterine biology in the lab using organoids (tiny living models of uterine tissue) to create more accurate, human-relevant tools for R&D discovery. By putting women's biology at the center of our research, we accelerate better diagnostics, safer therapies, and a deeper understanding of gynecological health.

title: The Missing Vector: Recalibrating Your Inner Compass
content:
There is no single definition of success or happiness—it is entirely your own. But true success has a distinct framework: you have the results, and you actually feel fulfilled. 

Too often, high-achievers master the external metrics while living with a subtle, persistent emptiness. This happens when we build from the head rather than the higher self, choosing paths that are logical but fundamentally not ours. Without an internal compass, how do you know if what you are building is actually aligned?

Your True North cannot be engineered by the mind or copied from a playbook. It is not something you invent; it is a frequency you allow yourself to be led by.

title: Path to Resolution (P2R): interactive workshop on peer-led conflict resolution models
content:
Path to Resolution (P2R) proposes a structured, peer-led conflict resolution model that turns tension into dialogue and dialogue into solutions. In this interactive workshop, you'll learn the basics of the model and contribute to building it.

Participants shape every stage of the process, including drafting community norms together, navigating real friction through anonymous posting, voluntary conversation, and peer-led accountability.

Expect to:
- Create your own community guidelines from scratch
- Practice each stage of P2R through live exercises and real scenarios
- Experience what peer-driven conflict resolution actually feels like
- Leave with a model you can bring back to your own community

No conflict resolution experience needed. Just bring your ideas and experiences. Family participation highly encouraged!

title: 1 hour Founder and Builder Listening Lab Sessions (2 sessions)
content:
We're creating several sessions for unique builders to come together. Our hypothesis is that - sometimes people who are a powerhouse in one way, with an unusual mind - and an inner spark - also come with some unusual features.

This is a space for these builders and those in relationship with them. It's a place to talk about the things we usually hide, race past, or dismiss as liabilities — and instead discuss how to leverage our uniqueness, in a way that breeds longevity. 

The core question: How can we root and adapt after Edge? 

Dara + Tierney are hosting real conversations: real interesting, real vulnerable, real useful. Together, we’ll explore delightfully bizarre building styles, what works, what concerns us, and what we desire most. And what teamwork has to do with it. Because we believe Neurodiverse founders are uniquely suited to thrive in the long term if approached intentionally/differently, and together.

title: Makerspace Open Hours
content:
The Edge Esmeralda makerspace is a prototyping space that lowers the barrier to building.

Open hours are a time for drop-in access where you can get help from a trained volunteer. We have 3D printers, sewing machines, a Cricut machine, computers, arts and crafts materials, and whatever else you want to contribute.

We are looking for more people to donate materials and tools, host open hours, or run workshops based on their interests. Please reach out to @dessertgrace and @Martine_Estuary on Telegram.

Makerspace Goals:
- Turn conversations into things
    - You have ideas. The makerspace has the tools and training to make them real.
- Create collisions
    - Strike up a conversation to find a collaborator or get unstuck. Attend programming focused on relationship building and multidisciplinary projects.
- Make it your own
    - The space is maintained by participants. Share your knowledge by running a workshop. Volunteer to help others’ ideas become real.

title: The Void
content:
A sacred pause in the schedule. The Void is intentional unstructured time - an invitation to step away from constant stimulation, productivity, networking, and planning, and reconnect with yourself, nature, rest, or whatever is quietly calling for your attention.

Maybe it’s taking a walk without your phone. Maybe it’s journaling, napping, sitting under a tree, making art, crying, daydreaming, or finally doing the thing you’ve been avoiding because you’ve been too busy. 

The Void is not empty - it’s where integration, intuition, creativity, and unexpected magic often emerge. Use this time however your nervous system and soul most need.

Sponsored by Jess Luibrand as Community Care Culture + Nico from Agartha

title: 1 Hour of Silence
content:
An invitation to step out of the noise and into stillness. For one hour, we honor silence - separately. No talking, no phones, no networking, no pressure to perform or engage. Just space to breathe, notice, reflect, and reconnect with yourself beneath the constant movement of the day.

You’re welcome to meditate, journal, walk slowly, rest, stretch, or simply sit in quiet presence. In a world filled with endless input and stimulation, this hour is an experiment in listening - to the body, the mind, the environment, and the subtle wisdom that often only appears when things become quiet enough to hear it.

Hosted by Jess Luibrand, Community Care Culture Lead and Nico from Agartha

title: Ecstatic Dance
content:
A space to move freely, release what’s been held, and reconnect with the wisdom of the body through music and movement. Ecstatic Dance is an invitation to step out of the thinking mind and into presence - no choreography, no performance, no expectation, just authentic expression in a shared communal space.

Come as you are and move however your body wants to move: wild, soft, joyful, emotional, playful, grounded, or completely still. This is a judgment-free environment rooted in liberation, embodiment, and collective energy. Let the music guide you home to yourself.

In alignment with Ecstatic Dance rules: No talking, no touching!

Week 1: Hosted by Agartha Residency
Week 2-4: open to collaboration with DJ’s and Residencies! DM @jessluibrand on telegram
